title: sampling-shearbench-latency-cost-histogram-notes-2028-07-03
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note records an experimental run I called 'shearbench' — a focused sampling-based microbenchmark designed to expose the shape (not just percentiles) of latency and cost under mixed sustained + microburst traffic. The goal is a compact, reproducible text-first collateral piece we can copy into a one-pager or deck.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Under the tested config, small sustained load (10 qps) with infrequent short bursts (200 qps for 3s every ~120s) produced a bimodal latency histogram with two clear modes: ~18–25ms (steady) and ~180–260ms (burst-affected).
- Cost per query (amortized token cost including idle amortization) rose ~12% when burst preemption/slot contention occurred vs the no-burst baseline.
- Sampling the latency distribution at 100ms bins and overlaying token-cost heatmap reveals which bins contribute most to cost regressions (long tail >200ms despite low volume).

Environment and hardware:
- Runtime: redwood-serving-runtime v3.7.1-shearprov
- Model: open-vicuna-13b-quant (int8 profile A)
- Instance: g4x2-like GPU pool (2x A100-sim equivalent), 32GB RAM per node
- Autoscaling: slot-based, max_concurrency_per_slot=8, slot_duration=30s, standby_slots=2
- KV cache: enabled, ttl 90s, hitrate observed ~72% for our test prompt mix

Workload and test harness:
- Query mix: 60% short prompts (<=40 tokens), 30% medium (40-120 tokens), 10% long (>120 tokens)
- Token generation target: 40 tokens per response average
- Baseline profile: steady 10 qps sustained for 30m
- Burst profile: every 120s inject 3s spike @200 qps (poisson arrival within spike window)
- Duration: 30m per run, 3 runs per configuration (random seeds differ)
- Client harness: shearbench-client v0.9 (node), records per-request: start_ts, end_ts, qps_bucket_tag, tokens_out, model_variant

Data captured (primary fields):
- latency_ms (end_ts - start_ts)
- tokens_out
- slot_acquired (bool)
- preempted (bool)
- kv_cache_hit (bool)
- cost_estimated_cents (derived, includes amortized idle cost share)

Methodology notes (sampling rationale):
- Rather than storing every request over long runs, we sampled at 10% uniformly but forced capture for any request with latency>100ms or tokens_out>100. This hybrid sampling amplifies rare tail events while keeping dataset size manageable.
- Sampling weight recorded so histograms can be unbiased-corrected in postprocessing.
- We also kept a separate high-resolution capture (full logging) for one 5-minute window per run to validate that sampling correction faithfully reconstructs the heavy tail.

Representative text charts (ascii-friendly)
1) Latency histogram (100ms bins, corrected weights) — counts normalized per 1000 requests

[0-100)ms  | █████████████████████████████  (870)
[100-200)ms| ████                         (95)
[200-300)ms| ████                         (85)
[300-500)ms| ██                           (30)
[500-1000)ms| █                            (10)
>1000ms    |                              (0)

Interpretation: steady-mode dominates (0-100ms), but a non-trivial secondary mode sits between 100-300ms that accounts for ~18% of cost-weighted latency.

2) Cost heatmap by latency bin (amortized cents per request, avg tokens constant):
[0-100)ms   : $0.011 per request
[100-200)ms : $0.014 per request
[200-300)ms : $0.019 per request
[300-500)ms : $0.031 per request
>500ms      : $0.078 per request

Note: even though >300ms bins are rare in volume, they are disproportionately expensive because they coincide with slot preemption and fallback retries in our simulated routing.

3) Time series snapshot (p90 latency and instantaneous qps) — sampled 1s step, 2-minute window with an injected spike at t=40s

Time(s) | qps | p90_latency_ms
   0    | 10  | 22
  10    | 10  | 20
  30    | 12  | 23
  40    | 200 | 245   <-- burst window start
  41    | 200 | 260
  42    | 200 | 240
  44    | 65  | 180   <-- tail lingering as slots drain
  60    | 12  | 28
 120    | 10  | 22

Short commentary: spikes push p90 up into the 200–260ms band immediately; tail effects persist for tens of seconds due to slot reclamation and backend cold penalties.

Findings and actionable hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Increasing standby_slots from 2 -> 4 reduces headroom loss during bursts and halves the >200ms mass in the histogram. (cheap experiment to run)
- Hypothesis B: Aggressive KV cache warming for tenants with periodic bursts reduces both latency and cost because token generation remains on faster execution paths; measure by warming TTL to 300s for the next run.
- Hypothesis C: Dynamic slot prioritization (burst-affine slots) might mitigate preemption-induced retries; requires change in scheduler.

Quick experiment plan (next week):
1) Repeat baseline with standby_slots=4 (3 runs). Record same sampling fields.
2) Run TTL=300s KV cache policy (measure hitrate delta).
3) Add an experiment where we bind bursts only to a subset of slots (slot pool A) to see isolated queueing dynamics.

Notes to self / open questions:
- We saw a handful of preempted==true records correlated with >400ms latency and cost spikes. Need more logs from runtime: reason codes for preemption (OOM vs scheduling).
- Does autoscaler backfill empty slots in <10s? Observed ~18s in one trace. If so, that explains lingering tail. File issue to SRE with trace ids.
- Should annotate the ascii charts with sample counts per bin (done above) before I hand off to docs.

Suggested collateral outputs:
- One-page "shearbench" brief with the two ascii charts, 3 bullets of findings, and the 3 recommended experiments.
- A tiny heatmap graphic (generated from the CSV) for the product deck. Keep text-version for Slack/PR notes.

Appendix: small raw table (sample-corrected averages)
Rows: latency_bin | fraction_of_volume | fraction_of_cost | avg_cost_cents | avg_tokens
[0-100)ms  | 0.82 | 0.65 | 1.1 | 38
[100-200)ms| 0.09 | 0.14 | 1.4 | 41
[200-300)ms| 0.07 | 0.11 | 1.9 | 49
[300+ms    | 0.02 | 0.10 | 3.1 | 60

Logging pointers / links:
- shearbench client repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/shearbench
- runtime logs (sampled traces): s3://redwood-logs/obs/shearbench/2028-07-03/run3/trace-ids.txt
- follow-up ticket: JIRA-OBS-719 (investigate slot backfill behavior)

Status: draft. I'll run the standby_slots experiment next and update this doc with new ascii charts and the small PNG heatmap.

-- Asha
